_comment: Hand-curated aliases for tools/terms that ESCO has no dedicated skill for, or only under a much broader label. NOT touched by scripts/build-esco-taxonomy.mjs — kept deliberately separate from the generated esco-taxonomy.json so rebuilding the taxonomy from a newer ESCO export never overwrites these. Each key is matched as a normalized (lowercased, punctuation-stripped) whole phrase against resume/job text; each value is the skill's stable ESCO Concept URI (http://data.europa.eu/esco/skill/...) — NOT a compact skill:N id. skill:N ids are just a build-time incrementing counter over whichever skills survive scripts/build-esco-taxonomy.mjs's category filter that run, so they silently shift on every rebuild whenever the filter itself changes (this is exactly what broke SAP/credit-risk/MIS/Excel/Pandas after the HR carve-out was added — the aliases kept pointing at whatever skill happened to land on the same number afterward). A Concept URI is ESCO's own permanent identifier for the concept and never changes across rebuilds, so it's the only safe thing to pin an alias to. server/services/escoTaxonomyService.js resolves each URI to the current build's skill:N id at server startup (and throws if a URI isn't found in the current taxonomy); scripts/build-esco-client-bundle.mjs does the same at client-bundle build time; scripts/build-esco-taxonomy.mjs also validates every URI here against its freshly-built taxonomy and fails the build if one is missing, so a stale or typo'd URI can never ship silently again. See README.md's ESCO section for how this file is used.
